investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict) — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: Every attempt by the AURA observability eval to create a new remote agent via POST /api/agents is immediately rejected with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", preventing the runner from obtaining an agentId, vmId, or remoteState. All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the identical error message, confirming the failure originates at the shared agent-creation step before any downstream lifecycle or runtime logic is reached.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard per-org (or per-environment) agent quota of 100 and is refusing all new agent creation requests with a 409 conflict response. Because the eval runner calls createAgent() as the very first substantive step for every remote-agents check (run-status-probes.mjs line 1859), none of the three checks can proceed past agent creation, and zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is collected. This is an eval-observable signal that the production-api swarm backend's agent quota for the probe org is at or above its limit of 100; it is not confirmed to be a broad user-facing outage without additional traffic or incident evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — the runner never advanced past the failed createAgent() call
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical 409 message, latencyMs=1057, evidenceKeys=[] — confirms the same upstream failure
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical 409 message, latencyMs=917, evidenceKeys=[] — confirms the same upstream failure

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1851-1859: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1859 as the first operation; a 409 here terminates the probe before any evidence can be written

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because agent creation failed
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1141 — the check resolved in ~1 second, consistent with an immediate API rejection rather than a timeout or slow provisioning path
possibleCauses: Most likely: the probe org's swarm agent count has reached or exceeded the enforced limit of 100, causing every new POST /api/agents to be rejected. This could result from prior eval runs that created agents without successfully cleaning them up (withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs line 1857 may not have run if earlier runs crashed before cleanup).
Possible: a previous eval run left orphaned remote agents in the probe org that were never deleted, gradually consuming quota until the limit was hit.
Possible: the quota limit of 100 was recently lowered on the swarm backend for the probe org or environment, causing previously-passing runs to start failing.
Less likely: the probe org credentials or org scoping changed such that the eval is now targeting a different org that already has 100 agents, rather than a dedicated low-population probe org.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval suite blocked by swarm agent quota exhaustion on POST /api/agents (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T06:36:33–35Z with the identical 409 response "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval runner's call to POST /api/agents was rejected before any agent could be created or polled. Because agent creation is the first step in the remote-agent-state probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1879: createAgent), no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever collected, causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard per-org agent quota of 100. At the time the eval ran, that quota was already at or above the limit, so every POST /api/agents call returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval probe for remote-agent-state calls createAgent as its very first action (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1879), the 409 caused an immediate failure before any state polling or evidence collection could occur. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition in the production swarm backend; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm backend rejected agent creation due to quota exhaustion.

sibling.remote-agent-create and sibling.remote-agent-runtime carry the identical 409 message (evidenceItems sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime), establishing that all three remote-agents checks share the same upstream failure point.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent, consistent with the probe never advancing past the createAgent call (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1871-1879, line 1879).
failed-check.evidence is an empty object {}, confirming zero evidence was written before the check terminated.

verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure is true, and all sameMessageSiblingIds match, pointing to a single shared upstream dependency (POST /api/agents) rather than independent per-check failures.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266 (line 264) confirms the contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none of which could be populated when createAgent fails immediately.
possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm org-scoped agent quota is at or above the hard limit of 100 at the time the eval runs. Prior eval runs or other processes created agents that were not cleaned up, leaving the quota exhausted. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1877) is only reached if createAgent succeeds; a 409 on creation means cleanup of the new agent never runs, but previously leaked agents from earlier failed runs may have accumulated.

Secondary — A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted before its cleanup callback could delete the agent it created, incrementally consuming quota over multiple runs. The history object shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, meaning no baseline passing state is recorded, which is consistent with quota having been exhausted before this run window began.

Tertiary (lower confidence) — The eval probe account or org is shared with non-eval workloads that independently created agents up to the quota limit, leaving no headroom for the observability probes.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-06-19T06:36:33–35Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached for the eval org. investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected every POST /api/agents call with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". This is an upstream resource-limit condition on the eval org's swarm agent quota, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. Because createAgent() fails immediately, the eval probe never reaches the runtime-test or state-polling stages, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) unpopulated and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict) — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: Every attempt by the AURA observability eval to create a new remote agent via POST /api/agents is immediately rejected with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", preventing the runner from obtaining an agentId, vmId, or remoteState. All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the identical error message, confirming the failure originates at the shared agent-creation step before any downstream lifecycle or runtime logic is reached.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard per-org (or per-environment) agent quota of 100 and is refusing all new agent creation requests with a 409 conflict response. Because the eval runner calls createAgent() as the very first substantive step for every remote-agents check (run-status-probes.mjs line 1859), none of the three checks can proceed past agent creation, and zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is collected. This is an eval-observable signal that the production-api swarm backend's agent quota for the probe org is at or above its limit of 100; it is not confirmed to be a broad user-facing outage without additional traffic or incident evidence.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — the runner never advanced past the failed createAgent() call

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical 409 message, latencyMs=917, evidenceKeys=[] — confirms the same upstream failure

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because agent creation failed
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1141 — the check resolved in ~1 second, consistent with an immediate API rejection rather than a timeout or slow provisioning path
possibleCauses: Most likely: the probe org's swarm agent count has reached or exceeded the enforced limit of 100, causing every new POST /api/agents to be rejected. This could result from prior eval runs that created agents without successfully cleaning them up (withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs line 1857 may not have run if earlier runs crashed before cleanup).
Possible: a previous eval run left orphaned remote agents in the probe org that were never deleted, gradually consuming quota until the limit was hit.
Possible: the quota limit of 100 was recently lowered on the swarm backend for the probe org or environment, causing previously-passing runs to start failing.
Less likely: the probe org credentials or org scoping changed such that the eval is now targeting a different org that already has 100 agents, rather than a dedicated low-population probe org.

investigations.title: Remote Agents eval suite blocked by swarm agent quota exhaustion on POST /api/agents (HTTP 409)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T06:36:33–35Z with the identical 409 response "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval runner's call to POST /api/agents was rejected before any agent could be created or polled. Because agent creation is the first step in the remote-agent-state probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1879: createAgent), no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever collected, causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard per-org agent quota of 100. At the time the eval ran, that quota was already at or above the limit, so every POST /api/agents call returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval probe for remote-agent-state calls createAgent as its very first action (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1879), the 409 caused an immediate failure before any state polling or evidence collection could occur. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition in the production swarm backend; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the swarm backend rejected agent creation due to quota exhaustion.

sibling.remote-agent-create and sibling.remote-agent-runtime carry the identical 409 message (evidenceItems sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime), establishing that all three remote-agents checks share the same upstream failure point.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent, consistent with the probe never advancing past the createAgent call (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1871-1879, line 1879).
failed-check.evidence is an empty object {}, confirming zero evidence was written before the check terminated.

verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure is true, and all sameMessageSiblingIds match, pointing to a single shared upstream dependency (POST /api/agents) rather than independent per-check failures.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266 (line 264) confirms the contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none of which could be populated when createAgent fails immediately.
possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm org-scoped agent quota is at or above the hard limit of 100 at the time the eval runs. Prior eval runs or other processes created agents that were not cleaned up, leaving the quota exhausted. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1877) is only reached if createAgent succeeds; a 409 on creation means cleanup of the new agent never runs, but previously leaked agents from earlier failed runs may have accumulated.

Secondary — A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted before its cleanup callback could delete the agent it created, incrementally consuming quota over multiple runs. The history object shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, meaning no baseline passing state is recorded, which is consistent with quota having been exhausted before this run window began.

Tertiary (lower confidence) — The eval probe account or org is shared with non-eval workloads that independently created agents up to the quota limit, leaving no headroom for the observability probes.

If the agent count for the eval probe org is found to be well below 100 when queried directly, the quota-exhaustion root cause would be disproved and the 409 would suggest a different conflict condition (e.g., duplicate agent name, org-level policy, or a backend bug).

If only one of the three sibling checks fails on a subsequent run while the others pass, the shared-dependency hypothesis would be weakened and the failure would be localized to a single check's logic rather than the shared createAgent call.

If the eval probe account belongs to an org that has never had agents created by other workloads and the quota counter is at 100 despite no visible agents, it would suggest a quota accounting bug in the swarm backend rather than genuine resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check (e.g., remote-agent-quota-headroom) that queries the agent count for the eval probe org before any creation attempt and fails with a clear quota-headroom message if fewer than N slots remain.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no eval-created agents persist in the probe org after a full probe run, catching cleanup regressions before they accumulate into quota exhaustion.
Add a remote-agents eval run that explicitly tests the cleanup path: create an agent, verify it exists, delete it, and verify it is gone — ensuring the withCleanup wrapper is exercised end-to-end.

Because agent creation is the first step in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1892), no agent was ever provisioned, so zero required evidence fields were collected and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime could not be satisfied.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected every POST /api/agents call with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". This is an upstream resource-limit condition on the eval org's swarm agent quota, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. Because createAgent() fails immediately, the eval probe never reaches the runtime-test or state-polling stages, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) unpopulated and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
